newsitem.title: USA: EU offers US temporary plan for poultry import reg.
newsitem.headline: EU offers US temporary plan for poultry import reg.

text.p: The European Union has offered the United States a "temporary solution" for poultry import standards until a long-term solution can be worked out, a senior EU official said on Wednesday.

Briefing reporters after two days of negotiations between the United States and the EU on a long-running meat inspection dispute, Lars Hoelgaard said the plan "would be of some months" to allow the U.S. poultry industry to make adjustments in its processing plants that the EU has requested.
Hoelgaard would not give any details of the EU's proposal, but said negotiators would be discussing the plan later today.

Hoelgaard is heading the EU team that is negotiating an agreement over the so-called veterinary equivalency rules. The transatlantic dispute has run for years, and the deadline by which to reach an agreement is looming on April 1.

An agreement would allow the United States and the European Union to accept meat, poultry, dairy products and pet food from each other even if they disagree on the particulars of how to assure the product is safe.
Hoelgaard said if the United States does not agree to the EU proposal on poultry, U.S. poultry and dairy exports to the EU could be disrupted after April 1.

The EU recently cut by 30 percent its list of U.S. poultry plants that meet its safety requirements. Hoelgaard said that "some adjustments are necessary" for U.S. poultry plants, even under the proposed temporary solution.

Hoelgaard acknowledged that poultry remains the main sticking point in the talks, and stressed that without an agreement, the EU harmonizing requirement would go into effect on April 1 and said this could create difficulty for U.S. poultry, dairy and eggs.
With regards to red meat trade, Hoelgaard maintained that the 1992 red meat agreement will continue after April 1, and said that beef and pork trade should be unaffected.

The administration and the U.S. meat industry have claimed that the EU has not treated U.S. meat exports fairly, and that while the United States has been willing to recognize equivalent EU standards, the EU has not done the same for the United States.
The EU official also said that most of the issues surrounding U.S. pet food exports to the EU had been resolved.
